-1 indicates the last entity

entries.name: qEntityFilter
entries.description: A query for entities in a queryToFilter which match a given EntityType.

entries.name: qHasAttribute
entries.description: Query for all entities marked with an attribute with name name

entries.name: qHasAttribute
entries.description: Query for all entities in queryToFilter marked with an attribute with name name

entries.name: qHasAttributeWithValue
entries.description: Query for all entities marked with an attribute with name name and value exactly equal to value

entries.name: qHasAttributeWithValue
entries.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, name is string, value)
entries.description: Query for all entities in queryToFilter marked with an attribute with name name and value exactly equal to value

entries.name: qHasAttributeWithValueMatching
entries.description: Query for all entities marked with an attribute with name name and a map value matching every key-value pair in the provided attributePattern map.

parameters.name: attributePattern

entries.name: qHasAttributeWithValueMatching
entries.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, name is string, attributePattern is map)
entries.description: Query for all entities in queryToFilter marked with an attribute with name name and a map value matching every key-value pair in the provided attributePattern map.

parameters.name: attributePattern

entries.name: qAttributeFilter
entries.description: Note: This query is used only for legacy unnamed attributes, which are still supported but no longer reccommended. See the Attributes module for details.

parameters.name: attributePattern
parameters.description:
Will only resolve to queries whose legacy unnamed attributes match the type (and possibly the values) of this pattern.
If attributePattern has a type tag, will only match attributes with that same type tag. 
EXAMPLE
{} as MyCustomType will match all attributes with type tag MyCustomTypeIf the attribute has no type tag (i.e. it is a standard type like string or map), will match all attributes with that same standard type. 
EXAMPLE
"asdf" will match all string attributes. EXAMPLE
{} will match all map attributes.If the attribute is a map, will only match maps which have identical values for every key-value pair in the pattern 
EXAMPLE
{ "odd" : true } matches all unnamed map attributes that have a field "odd" whose value is true. EXAMPLE
{ "odd" : true } as MyCustomType matches all unnamed map attributes with the that have a field "odd" whose value is true.

entries.name: qAttributeQuery
entries.description: Note: This query is used only for legacy unnamed attributes, which are still supported but no longer reccommended. See the Attributes module for details.

entries.name: qCreatedBy
entries.description: A query for all the entities created by a feature or operation. The feature is given by its feature id, which was passed into the the operation function in order to create the feature.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified feature. 
EXAMPLE
id + "extrude1"

entries.name: qCapEntity
entries.signature: (featureId is Id, capType is CapType, entityType is EntityType)
entries.description: A query for start/end cap vertex, edge, and face entities created by featureId. Cap entities are produced by extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and thicken features

entries.name: qNonCapEntity
entries.description: A query for vertex, edge, and face entities created by featureId that are not cap entities. Cap entities are produced by extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and thicken features

entries.name: qOpHoleProfile
entries.description: A query for the profile edges or vertices created by an opHole operation.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified operation. 
EXAMPLE
id + "hole1"

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for profiles with a given name. See name field of HoleProfile.

parameters.name: identity
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for the hole associated with the given identity entity. See identities parameter of opHole.

entries.name: qOpHoleFace
entries.description: A query for the hole faces created by an opHole operation.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified operation. 
EXAMPLE
id + "hole1"

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for faces with a given name. See faceNames field of HoleDefinition.

parameters.name: identity
parameters.description: OptionalFilter the query for the hole associated with the given identity entity. See identities parameter of opHole.

entries.name: qUnion
entries.description: A query for entities which match any of a list of queries.

entries.name: qUnion
entries.signature: (query1 is Query, query2 is Query, query3 is Query)

entries.name: qUnion
entries.signature: (query1 is Query, query2 is Query, query3 is Query, query4 is Query)

entries.name: qIntersection
entries.description: A query for entities which match all of a list of queries. qIntersection preserves the order of the first subquery.

entries.name: qSubtraction
entries.description: A query for entities which match query1, but do not match query2. qSubtraction preserves the order of query1.

entries.name: qSymmetricDifference
entries.description: A query for entities which match either query1 or query2, but not both.

entries.name: qOwnedByBody
entries.description: A query for all of the entities (faces, vertices, edges, and bodies) in a context which belong to a specified body or bodies.

entries.name: qOwnedByBody
entries.description: A query for all of the entities which match a queryToFilter, and belong to the specified body or bodies.

entries.name: qOwnerBody
entries.description: A query for each body that any of the given entities belong to.

entries.name: qContainedInCompositeParts
entries.description: A query for each part contained in compositeParts.

entries.name: qCompositePartsContaining
entries.description: A query for each composite part containing bodies.

entries.name: qCompositePartsContaining
entries.description: A query for each composite part of the given type containing bodies.

entries.name: qFlattenedCompositeParts
entries.description: A query for non-composite entities in entities and constituents of composite parts in entities.

entries.name: qConsumed
entries.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter which are consumed by any closed composite part, or all entities of queryToFilter which are not consumed by any closed composite part.

entries.name: qCompositePartTypeFilter
entries.description: A query for all bodies in queryToFilter which are either open or closed composite parts, depending on the second parameter.

entries.name: qSourceMesh
entries.description: A query for each mesh element that any selectedMeshVertices belong to. selectedMeshVertices should be the point bodies created when a user selects a mesh vertex. Mesh vertices which have not been selected cannot be queried in FeatureScript

parameters.name: selectedMeshVertices
parameters.description: One or more mesh vertices whose owning elements are queried.

entries.name: qSourceMesh
entries.description: Deprecated: Use qSourceMesh with EntityType.BODY

entries.name: qAdjacent
entries.signature: (seed is Query, adjacencyType is AdjacencyType, entityType is EntityType)
entries.description: A query for entities that are adjacent to the given seed entities.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: One or more entities whose adjacent neighbors are queried. The result does not include the original seed entities (unless they are adjacent to other seed entities)

entries.name: qVertexAdjacent
entries.description: Deprecated: Use qAdjacent with AdjacencyType.VERTEX

entries.name: qEdgeAdjacent
entries.description: Deprecated: Use qAdjacent with AdjacencyType.EDGE

entries.name: qEdgeTopologyFilter
entries.description: A query for edges in a queryToFilter which match a given EdgeTopology.

entries.name: qEdgeVertex
entries.description: A query for the start or end vertices of edges.

entries.name: qGeometry
entries.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter with a specified GeometryType.

entries.name: qBodyType
entries.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter which are bodies of the a specified BodyType, or are owned by bodies with the specified BodyType

entries.name: qBodyType
entries.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter with any of a list of BodyTypes.

entries.name: qConstructionFilter
entries.description: A query for all construction entities or all non-construction entities in queryToFilter.

entries.name: qActiveSheetMetalFilter
entries.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter belonging to an active sheet metal part.

entries.name: qSheetMetalFlatFilter
entries.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter belonging to a flattened sheet metal part.

entries.name: qSMFlatFilter
entries.description: Deprecated: Use qSheetMetalFlatFilter

entries.name: qSheetMetalFormFilter
entries.description: A query for all entities in queryToFilter that are artifacts of a sheet metal form feature on flat pattern.

entries.name: qPartsAttachedTo
entries.description: A query for parts to which sheetMetalEntities are attached (e.g. sheet metal bend line entities are attached to a flattened sheet metal part)

entries.name: qCorrespondingInFlat
entries.description: A query for entities in sheet metal flattened body corresponding to any entitiesInFolded which are part of 3D sheet metal bodies

entries.name: qSMDefinitionEntityFilter
entries.description: A query for sheet metal definition entities in a queryToFilter which match a given EntityType.

entries.name: qMeshGeometryFilter
entries.description: A query for all mesh entities or all non-mesh entities in queryToFilter.

entries.name: qModifiableEntityFilter
entries.description: A query for all modifiable entities in queryToFilter.

entries.name: qSketchFilter
entries.description: A query for all sketch entities, or all non-sketch entities in queryToFilter.

entries.name: qParallelPlanes
entries.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, referencePlane is Plane, allowAntiparallel is boolean)
entries.description: A query for all planar face entities that are parallel to the referencePlane.

parameters.name: referencePlane
parameters.description: The plane to reference when checking for parallelism.

parameters.name: allowAntiparallel
parameters.description: Whether to also return entities that are antiparallel.

entries.name: qParallelPlanes
entries.description: A query for all planar face entities in queryToFilter that are parallel to the referencePlane.

parameters.name: referencePlane
parameters.description: The plane to reference when checking for parallelism.

entries.name: qParallelPlanes
entries.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, normal is Vector, allowAntiparallel is boolean)
entries.description: A query for all planar face entities in queryToFilter that are parallel to a plane specified by the normal vector.

parameters.name: normal
parameters.description: The normal vector to reference when checking for parallelism.

parameters.name: allowAntiparallel
parameters.description: Whether to also return entities that are antiparallel.

entries.name: qPlanesParallelToDirection
entries.description: A query for all planar faces in queryToFilter that are parallel to the given direction vector (i.e., the plane normal is perpendicular to direction).

entries.name: qFacesParallelToDirection
entries.description: A query for all faces in queryToFilter that are parallel to the given direction vector e.g. if it is a planar face, the plane normal is perpendicular to direction if it is a cylindrical face, the axis is parallel to direction if it is an extruded face, the extrude direction is parallel to direction

entries.name: qParallelPlanes
entries.description: A query for all planar face entities in queryToFilter that are parallel to a plane specified by the normal vector.

parameters.name: normal
parameters.description: The normal vector to reference when checking for parallelism.

entries.name: qConvexConnectedFaces
entries.description: A query for a set of faces connected to seed via convex edges, flood-filling across any number of convex edges.

entries.name: qConcaveConnectedFaces
entries.description: A query for a set of faces connected to seed via concave edges, flood-filling across any number of concave edges.

entries.name: qTangentConnectedFaces
entries.description: A query for a set of faces connected to seed via tangent edges, flood-filling across any number of tangent edges.

entries.name: qTangentConnectedFaces
entries.description: A query for a set of faces connected to seed via tangent edges, flood-filling across any number of tangent edges.

entries.name: qTangentConnectedEdges
entries.description: A query for a chain of tangent edges connected to seed via tangent vertices, chaining across any number of tangent vertices.

entries.name: qLoopEdges
entries.description: A query for a set of edges defining a loop. If the seed has laminar edges, this query will extend to include all laminar loops that contain any seed edges. If the seed has faces, the result will include the loops forming the outer boundary of the joined faces.

entries.name: qParallelEdges
entries.description: A query for all linear edges in queryToFilter which are parallel (or anti-parallel) to the given direction.

entries.name: qParallelEdges
entries.description: A query to find all linear edges in queryToFilter which are parallel (or anti-parallel) to any linear edge in edges.

entries.name: qLoopBoundedFaces
entries.description: Given a face and an edge, query for all faces bounded by the given face, on the side of the given edge.

parameters.name: faceAndEdge
parameters.description: Should match a face and an edge. If multiple faces and edges match, used the first face and the first edge.

entries.name: qFaceOrEdgeBoundedFaces
entries.description: Given a seed face and bounding entities, matches all adjacent faces inside the bounding entities, expanding from the seed face.

parameters.name: faceAndBoundingEntities
parameters.description: A Query for the seed face, followed by any boundary faces or edges. The seed face must be first, so a qUnion should be used to guarantee the order.

entries.name: qHoleFaces
entries.description: Given a single face inside a hole or hole-like geometry, returns all faces of that hole.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: A query for a single face inside the hole.

entries.name: qSketchRegion
entries.description: A query for all fully enclosed, 2D regions created by a sketch.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description: The feature id of the Sketch being queried.

parameters.name: filterInnerLoops
parameters.description: OptionalSpecifies whether to exclude sketch regions fully contained in other sketch regions. A region whose border has a vertex or edge on the outside boundary is not considered "contained." Default is false.

entries.name: qUniqueVertices
entries.description: A query that filters out duplicate vertices. When duplicates are found, the vertex with the lowest deterministic ID is used.

entries.name: qMateConnectorsOfParts
entries.description: A query for all mate connectors owned by parts.

entries.name: qFilletFaces
entries.description: A query for fillet faces of radius equal to, less than or equal to, or greater than or equal to the input faces. If facesToCompareTo does not match one or more fillet faces, the resulting query will not match any faces. Will find the fillet radius from each face and compare to find faces of all fillets on that body that satisfy the compareType.

entries.name: qMatching
entries.description: Matches any faces or edges within owner bodies of entities in referenceEntities which are geometrically identical (same size and shape) to the face or edge in referenceEntities.

entries.name: qPatternInstances
entries.signature: (featureId is Id, instanceNames is array, entityType is EntityType)
entries.description: A query for entities created by a specific instance or instances of an opPattern operation.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
The Id of the specified feature. 
EXAMPLE
id + "pattern1"

parameters.name: instanceNames
parameters.description: The names of the instances to query for, a subset of the instanceNames passed into the opPattern operation.

entries.name: qPatternInstances
entries.signature: (featureId is Id, instanceName is string, entityType is EntityType)

entries.name: qDependency
entries.description: A query for the true dependency of the given dependentEntities. For instance, the true dependency of the extruded body will be the face or sketch edges of the profile from which it is extruded.

entries.name: qLaminarDependency
entries.description: A query for the true dependency of the given dependentEntities, specifically for use with wire edges that have been created from laminar edges. If the immediate dependency is not laminar then it will track back until it reaches a laminar dependency (if there is one).

entries.name: qContainsPoint
entries.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter containing a specified point.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: A 3D point, in world space.

entries.name: qIntersectsLine
entries.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter touching a specified infinite line.

entries.name: qIntersectsPlane
entries.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter touching a specified infinite plane.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * meter, vector(0, 0, 1))

entries.name: qInFrontOfPlane
entries.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter in front of a specified infinite plane. Entities intersecting the plane will not be resolved. Only entities completely on one side or coincident with the plane will be selected. Use flip(plane) to query entities on the other side of the plane. For example, for the XY plane through the origin with the normal (0, 0, 1), qInFrontOfPlane will resolve the vertices (1, 1, 0) and (1, 1, 1) but not the vertex (1, 1, -1).

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * meter, vector(0, 0, 1))

entries.name: qCoincidesWithPlane
entries.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges, or points) in queryToFilter coinciding with a specified infinite plane.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * meter, vector(0, 0, 1))

entries.name: qWithinRadius
entries.signature: (queryToFilter is Query, point is Vector, radius is ValueWithUnits)
entries.description: A query for all entities (bodies, faces, edges or points) in queryToFilter that are within a specified radius from a point.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: The point from which to check distance from.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.description: The distance away from the point.

entries.name: qClosestTo
entries.description: A query for the entity in queryToFilter closest to a point.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: A position vector for the point to find entities closest to.

entries.name: qFarthestAlong
entries.description: A query for the entity in queryToFilter farthest along a direction in world space. In the case of a tie, resolves to all entities within TOLERANCE.zeroLength of being the farthest.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: A vector for the direction to find the entity farthest away.

entries.name: qLargest
entries.description: A query to find the largest entity (by length, area, or volume) in queryToFilter.

entries.name: qSmallest
entries.description: A query to find the smallest entity (by length, area, or volume) in queryToFilter.

entries.name: qEdgeConvexityTypeFilter
entries.description: A query that filters given edges by convexity.

entries.name: qAxis
entries.description: A query that filters edges and faces into axis-symmetric ones (lines, circles, cylinders, cones, tori, revolved, mate connectors) that have the given axis. The sign of the axis direction does not matter.

entries.name: qSplitBy
entries.signature: (featureId is Id, entityType, backBody is boolean)
entries.description: Given the id of a split feature, get entities of a given EntityType on the front or the back side of the split. For a split by face or part, the front denotes the body in the direction of the split tool's surface normal, and the back denotes the body opposite the normal. For a split by isocline, the front denotes non-steep faces and edges, and the back denotes steep entities.

parameters.name: featureId
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
id + "split1"

parameters.name: backBody
parameters.description:
EXAMPLE
false indicates the entities in the front. EXAMPLE
true indicates the entities in the back.

entries.name: sketchEntityQuery
entries.signature: (operationId is Id, entityType, sketchEntityId is string)
entries.description: Gets the wire body entities created for a specific sketch entity. If the sketch id created multiple sketch entities, will return all the wire bodies.

parameters.name: operationId
parameters.description: Id of the sketch feature.

parameters.name: sketchEntityId
parameters.description: Sketch id.

entries.name: evaluateQuery
entries.description: Returns an array of queries for the individual entities in a context which match a specified query. The returned array contains exactly one transient query for each matching entity at the time of the call. If the context is modified, the returned queries may become invalid and no longer match an entity.

entries.name: areQueriesEquivalent
entries.signature: (context is Context, first is Query, second is Query)
entries.description: Returns true if the supplied queries evaluate to the same set of entities. This function is order-invariant, so if the two queries evaluate to the same entities, but in a different order, the function will still return true.

entries.name: isQueryEmpty
entries.description: Returns true if query evaluates to nothing. Equivalent to evaluateQuery(context, query) == [] or size(evaluateQuery(context, query)) == 0, but faster than either of those approaches if the query is not empty.

entries.name: evaluateQueryCount
entries.description: Returns the number of entities returned by the supplied query. Equivalent to size(evaluateQuery(context, query)), but faster.

files.description: Evaluation functions return information about the topological entities in the context, like bounding boxes, tangent planes, projections, and collisions. Evaluation functions take a context and a map that specifies the computation to be performed and return a ValueWithUnits, a FeatureScript geometry type (like Line or Plane), or a special type like DistanceResult. They may also throw errors if a query fails to evaluate or the input is otherwise invalid.

entries.name: evApproximateCentroid
entries.description: Find the centroid of an entity or group of entities. This is equivalent to the center of mass for a constant density object. Warning: This is an approximate value and it is not recommended to use this for modeling purposes that will be negatively affected in case the approximation changes. Consider using the center of a bounding box instead.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: The entities to take the center of mass of.

entries.name: MassProperties
entries.description: The result of an evApproximateMassProperties call.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Description

parameters.name: mass
parameters.description: The total mass.

parameters.name: centroid
parameters.description: The center of mass with respect to the given reference frame, or with respect to the origin if a reference frame is not specified.

parameters.name: inertia
parameters.description: The 3D inertia tensor, with units of mass * length ^ 2. Evaluated with respect to the reference frame, or with respect to the centroid if a reference frame is not specified.

parameters.name: volume
parameters.description: Total volume. Only returned for solid bodies.

parameters.name: area
parameters.description: Total area. Only returned for faces.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Total length. Only returned for edges.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Total count. Only returned for vertices.

entries.name: evApproximateMassProperties
entries.description: Calculates approximate mass properties of an entity or group of entities. Returns mass, centroid, inertia tensor, and volume/area/length/count for bodies/faces/edges/vertices, respectively. Warning: These are approximate values and it is not recommended to use them for modeling purposes that will be negatively affected in case the approximation changes.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: The entities of which to compute mass properties. Only entities of the highest dimensionality will be considered.

parameters.name: density
parameters.description:
The density of the entities, with appropriate units. 
EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram / meter ^ 3 could be the density of 3D solid bodies EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram / meter ^ 2 could be the density of 2D faces or sheet bodies EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram / meter could be the density of 1D edges or wire bodies EXAMPLE
1 * kilogram could be the mass of each 0D vertex or point body

parameters.name: referenceFrame
parameters.description: OptionalOptional coordinate system. Defaults to the centroid with world axes for the inertia tensor, and world coordinates for the centroid.

entries.name: evArea
entries.description: Return the total area of all the entities. If no matching 2D faces are found the total area will be zero.

entries.name: evAxis
entries.description: If the query finds one entity with an axis -- a line, circle, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, mate connector, or revolved surface -- return the axis. Otherwise throw an exception.

entries.name: evBox3d
entries.description: Find a bounding box around an entity, optionally with respect to a given coordinate system. There is also an option to use a faster but less accurate method.

parameters.name: topology
parameters.description: The entity to find the bounding box of.

parameters.name: cSys
parameters.description: OptionalThe coordinate system to use (if not the standard coordinate system).

parameters.name: tight
parameters.description:
OptionalGet the tightest possible bounding box. Defaults to true. 
EXAMPLE
true for a bounding box precisely at the extents of the given entities (and no bigger). EXAMPLE
false for a bounding box at least as big as the given entities, using a faster algorithm.

entries.name: evCollision
entries.description: Find collisions between tools and targets. Each collision is a map with field type of type ClashType and fields target, targetBody, tool, and toolBody of type Query.

entries.name: evCornerType
entries.description: Return the type of corner found at a vertex of a sheet metal model

parameters.name: Return
parameters.description: Description

parameters.name: primaryVertex
parameters.description: the vertex that defines the corner

parameters.name: allVertices
parameters.description: array of transient queries for all definition vertices associated with the corner

parameters.name: GBTErrorStringEnum.BAD_GEOMETRY
parameters.type: The query does not evaluate to a single vertex

entries.name: evCurveDefinition
entries.description: Given a query for a curve, return a Circle, Ellipse, Line, or BSplineCurve value for the curve. If the curve is none of these types, return a map with unspecified contents.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: The curve to evaluate.

parameters.name: returnBSplinesAsOther
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, do not return B-spline curves (to avoid the associated time cost). Default is false.

parameters.name: GBTErrorStringEnum.INVALID_INPUT
parameters.type: The first resolved entity was not an edge.

parameters.name: GBTErrorStringEnum.CANNOT_RESOLVE_ENTITIES
parameters.type: Input entities are invalid or there are no input entities.

entries.name: evApproximateBSplineCurve
entries.description: Given a query for a curve, return its approximation (or exact representation if possible) as a B-spline. The options forceCubic and forceNonRational may be used to restrict the type of spline that is returned, but even if these options are false, a cubic non-rational spline may be returned.

parameters.name: edge
parameters.description: The curve to approximate.

parameters.name: forceCubic
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, a cubic spline will be returned. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: forceNonRational
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, a non-rational spline will be returned. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: OptionalSpecifies the desired approximation tolerance: the maximum distance (in meters) between the original curve and the returned spline representation. Default is 1e-6, minimum is 1e-8, and maximum is 1e-2.

entries.name: DistanceResult
entries.description: The result of an evDistance call -- information about the extremal distance and the attaining point / line / entity.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Description

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: The minimal or maximal distance.

parameters.name: sides
parameters.description:
An array of 2 maps, containing information about where the extremum was found for each side. Each map has a:
point (Vector) : The position in world space that is closest or farthest to the other side. The distance field is measured between the two values of point.
index (integer) : the index into the line or point array or into the query results, if a query is passed in.
parameter (number or length or array of two numbers) : If the index refers to an edge, the parameter is a number between 0 and 1 (unless extend for that side was passed in). It is in the form that evEdgeTangentLine and evEdgeCurvature consume (with arcLengthParameterization set to the same value that was passed into evDistance).
If the index refers to a point, the parameter is 0.
If the index refers to a Line, the parameter is a length representing the distance along the direction.
If the index refers to a face, the parameter is a 2D Vector in the form that evFaceTangentPlane consumes. If this face is a mesh or a plane, the parameter is a 2D Vector of zeroes.
If the index refers to a Plane, the parameter is a 2D Vector representing the lengths along the plane's x and y axes.

entries.name: evDistance
entries.description: Computes the minimum or maximum distance between geometry on side0 and geometry on side1. "Geometry" means entities, points, or lines. When the minimum or the maximum is not uniquely defined, ties will be broken arbitrarily.

parameters.name: side0
parameters.description:
One of the following: A query, or a point (3D Length Vector), or a Line, or a Plane, or an array of points, or an array of Lines, or an array of Planes. 
EXAMPLE
qNthElement(qEverything(EntityType.FACE), 0) or vector(1, 2, 3) * meter or line(vector(1, 0, 1) * meter, vector(1, 1, 1) or plane(vector(1,1,1) * meter, vector(0,0,1), vector(1,0,0)).

parameters.name: extendSide0
parameters.description: OptionalIf true and side0 is a query, bodies will be ignored and edges and faces extended to their possibly infinite underlying surfaces. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: side1
parameters.description: Like side0.

parameters.name: extendSide1
parameters.description: OptionalLike extendSide0.

parameters.name: maximum
parameters.description: OptionalIf true, compute the maximum instead of the minimum. Defaults to false. Not allowed to be true if a line is passed in in either side or if either extend is true.

entries.name: RaycastResult
entries.description: Map containing the results of one collision between a ray and an entity.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Description

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: A query for the entity hit by the ray.

parameters.name: parameter
parameters.description: Parameters for where the ray hit the entity. A unitless 2-vector for a face, a number for an edge, else undefined.

parameters.name: intersection
parameters.description: Intersection point.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Distance of the intersection point from the ray origin.

entries.name: evRaycast
entries.description: Detect intersections between a ray and the given entities.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: A query for target entities. If bodies are provided, the result will contain intersections for individual entities owned by the body.

parameters.name: ray
parameters.description:
The ray to intersect the entities. Because the passed-in Line is interpreted as a ray, by default, intersections with entities "behind" the ray origin are not detected. includeIntersectionsBehind can be set to true if those intersections are desired. 
EXAMPLE
line(vector(0, 0, 0) * inch, vector(1, 0, 0)) specifies the positive x-axis

parameters.name: closest
parameters.description: OptionalGet only the closest intersection with any of the entities. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: includeIntersectionsBehind

parameters.description: Whether the spline is periodic.

parameters.name: controlPoints
parameters.description:
An array of control points. See BSplineCurve for specific detail. For periodic splines, you may provide the necessary overlap, or provide control points without any overlap. If no overlap is provided, degree overlapping control points (corresponding to the first degree control points) will be added to the end of the control points list (unless you provide a set of knots that show no overlap is necessary). 
EXAMPLE
[vector(-1, 1, 0) * inch, vector(1, 1, 0) * inch, vector(1, -1, 0) * inch, vector(-1, -1, 0) * inch]

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description: OptionalAn array of weights. See BSplineCurve for specific detail.

parameters.name: knots
parameters.description: OptionalAn array of knots. See BSplineCurve for specific detail. If knots are not provided a uniform parameterization wil be created such that the curve exists on the parameter range [0, 1]. For non-periodic curves with n control points, you may provide the full set of n + degree + 1 knots, or you may provide n - degree + 1 knots, and multiplicity will by padded onto the ends (which has the effect of clamping the spline to its two endpoints). For periodic curves with n unique control points (and optionally an additional degree overlapping control points), you may provide the full set of n + 2 * degree + 1 knots, or you may provide n + 1 knots, and the periodic knots will be padded onto the ends.

The resulting splines are consistently parameterized, so that, for example, lofting between them will match corresponding target positions. Note: If parameters are not specified, the magnitude of start and end derivatives in targets is ignored as well as the second component parallel with the first derivative.

If specified, the output spline at those parameters will match the target points. If specified, derivatives in approximation targets will not be rescaled.

parameters.name: controlPoints
parameters.description:
A matrix of control points. See BSplineSurface for specific detail. If u or v is periodic, you may provide the necessary overlap, or provide control points without any overlap. If no overlap is provided, degree overlapping control point rows or columns (corresponding to the first degree control point rows or columns) will be added. (unless you provide a set of knots that show no overlap is necessary). 
EXAMPLE
controlPointMatrix([
    [vector(-1, -1, -1) * inch, vector(-1, 0, 0) * inch, vector(-1, -2, 1) * inch],
    [vector( 0,  1, -1) * inch, vector( 0, 2, 0) * inch, vector( 0,  0, 1) * inch],

If knots are not provided a uniform parameterization will be created such that the u parameterization exists on the range [0, 1]. For non-periodic u with n control point rows, you may provide the full set of n + degree + 1 knots, or you may provide n - degree + 1 knots, and multiplicity will by padded onto the ends (which has the effect of clamping the surface to the control points in the first and last rows). For periodic u with n unique control points (and optionally an additional degree overlapping control points), you may provide the full set of n + 2 * degree + 1 knots, or you may provide n + 1 knots, and the periodic knots will be padded onto the ends.

files.description: Attributes are data attached to individual entities, which can be set and retrieved by name in FeatureScript. The data can be of any type, and multiple attributes with different names can be associated with the same topological entity.

entries.name: setAttribute
entries.description: Attach an attribute to one or several entities. Will overwrite any attribute previously set on the same entity with the same name.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: Entities to attach attribute to. Throws an error if the query resolves to nothing.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute

parameters.name: attribute
parameters.description:
The data to set. Can be any type. If undefined is provided, any existing attribute will be unset (and this entity will no longer resolve in qHasAttribute and similar functions) 
Legacy unnamed attributes: If name is not provided, adds an unnamed attribute to the entities. If more than one unnamed attribute with the same type is set on any entity, throws an error.

entries.name: getAttributes
entries.description: Get attributes attached to entities.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: Entities to get attributes on. If query resolves to nothing, empty array is returned

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to get.

parameters.name: attributePattern
parameters.description:
OptionalProviding a map here will also filter out attributes which do not have entries precisely matching the keys and values of attributePattern, similar to qHasAttributeWithValueMatching. 
EXAMPLE
{ "odd" : true } matches all attributes values are maps with a field "odd" whose value is true.Legacy unnamed attributes: If attributePattern is provided and name is not, getAttributes will only return unnamed attributes with the same type as attributePattern, using the same behavior documented in the legacy function qAttributeFilter.

parameters.name: array
parameters.type: An array of all unique attributes on the given entities matching the pattern.

entries.name: getAttribute
entries.description: Get the value of a single named attribute attached to a single entity, or undefined if no attribute of that name has been set.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: Query resolving to a single entity to get the attribute from. If multiple entities are resolved, the first resolved entity is considered.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the attribute

entries.name: getAllAttributes
entries.description: Get the named attributes attached to a single entity, or an empty map if the entity has no attributes.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: Query resolving to a single entity to get the attributes from.

parameters.name: map
parameters.type: A map from attribute names to attribute values for all of the attributes on the given entity.

entries.name: removeAttributes
entries.description: Has no effect on named attributes, instead use setAttribute with "attribute" : undefined.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description: OptionalEntities to remove unnamed attributes from. Default is everything.

parameters.name: attributePattern
parameters.description: OptionalIf provided, will only remove attributes with the same type, using the same behavior documented in the legacy function qAttributeFilter.

entries.name: memoizeFunction
entries.description: Memoize a unary (one-parameter) function. Once memoized, if the returned function is called with the same parameter twice, the second return value will be fetched from an internal cache. This can dramatically speed up calculations - particularly when f is called with the same parameter many times. The overhead of memoizing a function is negligible. Note that memoization will not properly work with functions that have side effects, such as modifying a box.

parameters.name: newNode

parameters.description: A unique id to represent the decal in the context of the face on which it is placed. The id should correspond to the id of the creating feature, or be a sub-id of the creating feature.

parameters.description: The image that is being mapped.

parameters.name: uvTransform
parameters.description: A post-projection transformation that is applied in UV space. This can be used to further translate, rotate, and scale a projected image.

parameters.name: planeSystem
parameters.description: OptionalA coordinate system representing the plane for the ImageMappingType.PLANAR type. This field must be defined if the imageMappingType field is of type ImageMappingType.PLANAR. The lower-left corner of the image will project to the plane's origin. The right edge of the image is along the positive X direction of the coordinate system. The top edge of the image is along the positive Y direction of the coordinate system. See planeToCSys for deriving a coordinate system from a Plane object.

parameters.name: cylinder
parameters.description: OptionalThe cylinder onto which the decal is mapped. This field must be defined if the imageMappingType field is of type ImageMappingType.CYLINDRICAL.

parameters.name: cylinderSystem
parameters.description: OptionalA coordinate system used in projecting the image onto the given cylinder. This field must be defined if the imageMappingType field is of type ImageMappingType.CYLINDRICAL. The coordinate system's origin must lie on the cylinder's axis with the system's Z axis aligned with the cylinder's own axis. The center of the horizontal extents of the image coincide with the intersection of the coordinate system's x axis and the cylinder. The center of the vertical extents of the image coincide with the projection of the coordinate system's origin on the cylinder. The top edge of the image is along the positive Z direction of the coordinate system projected on the cylinder.

A map of default parameter values for when this feature is called in FeatureScript.
This does NOT control the user-visible default value when creating this feature. To change the user-visible default for booleans, enums, and strings, use the "Default" annotation. To change the user-visible default for a length, angle, or number, see the valueBounds module.
EXAMPLE
{} will not modify the definition. EXAMPLE
{ "shouldFillet" : false } will set the parameter "shouldFillet" to false if the feature is called from FeatureScript without the "shouldFillet" parameter.

entries.name: setDimensionedEntities
entries.description: Tolerant dimensions require multiple pieces of information. This function specifies all of the information required for a dimension that cannot be specified in a tolerant quantity. Tolerant quantities are commonly declared in a feature using the UIHint.CAN_BE_TOLERANT or UIHint.CAN_BE_TOLERANT_DIAMETER UI hints in the annotation of the quantity parameter.

parameters.name: parameterId
parameters.description: The id of the tolerant quantity parameter in the feature definition.

parameters.name: queries
parameters.description: An array of one query (for a radius or diameter dimension) or two queries (for other dimensions). The queries can evaluate to more than one face, but in that case each face should lie on the same underlying surface. See extrude and fillet for examples.

parameters.name: facePairs
parameters.description: Required if queries is undefinedAn array of pairs of queries (a pair is an array of two queries). Used for features where mulitple face pairs are subject to the same constraint but they are not all coincident, for example, a thin extrusion of a square where the thickness is tolerant.

parameters.name: measuresSolidAngle
parameters.description: OptionalUsed to specify which part of a circle an angle dimension refers to. The angle between two planes can be defined by two possible numbers that sum to 360 degrees. If this option is SOLID, then the angle is measured from the first face, in to the part. If this option is VOID, then the angle is measured from the first face, out of the part. If this option is not set for an angle, then the result is consistent but undefined. It is recommended that an option is always provided for angle dimensions.

parameters.name: measurementDirection
parameters.description: OptionalUsed with dimensions of type FeatureDimensionType.AXIS_DISTANCE. If this option is not set then the dimension measures the shortest distance between the axes. If this option is set then the dimension measures the distance between the axes in this direction.

parameters.name: schemaClass
parameters.description: OptionalOn regeneration a dimension with a quantity with tolerance type ToleranceType.DEFAULT will set its tolerances given the nominal value and any default tolerances specified on the part. If this field is not set then the rule used will be either the default linear or angular rule, depending on the dimension type. If this field is set then the dimension will use the custom rule corresponding to the value. This field can also be a ToleranceSchemaClass to use a predefined class from the standard library. For example, you can set this to ToleranceSchemaClass.FILLET_RADIUS to use the same tolerance rules as Onshape's official fillet feature.

parameters.name: tolerances
parameters.description: OptionalContains tolerance and precision information for the specified parameter. This cannot be set if the parameter has been marked tolerant by the user.

parameters.name: nominal
parameters.description: Required if tolerances is not undefinedRequired if setting tolerances, for either an existing or new parameter. For an existing feature parameter, this is usually the value of that parameter.

entries.name: HoleDefinition
entries.description: Describes the shape of a hole using a series of HoleProfiles.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Description

parameters.name: profiles
parameters.description: An array of HoleProfiles which define the shape of the hole. The profiles are interpreted in order, from the top to the bottom of the hole. The final profile must have a radius of 0. Each profile must specify a unique name, or all of the profiles must leave their name field undefined. If two or more adjacent profiles in the list end up being identical (in the same position with the same radius) when their final placement is determined in opHole, the identical profiles will be collapsed into a single profile, which uses the name of the first of the identical profiles.

parameters.name: faceNames
parameters.description: OptionalA list of names to assign to the faces created by opHole. Should be the same length as the profiles array, where faceNames[i] is the name of the face created between profiles i - 1 and i, and faceNames[0] is the name of the top cap face (the face before profile 0). If any profiles are collapsed, the names of the faces between the collapsed profiles are skipped. Supplying faceNames allows for the querying of faces by name when using qOpHoleFace.

files.description: The instantiator makes it easy to efficiently bring in (possibly configured) bodies from other Part Studios and place them at specific positions and orientations. The usage pattern is generally as follows:

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The root id for all instances that will be created by this instantiator. Multiple instantiators can be used simultaneously, as long as they have different ids.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional

parameters.name: partQuery
parameters.description: OptionalThe query for all bodies to be brought in from the part studios. Default is all bodies except sketches.

parameters.name: tolerances
parameters.description:
OptionalThe tolerances for variable configuration inputs. Default is 1e-8 meters for lengths, 1e-11 radians for angles, and 0 for numbers. The default tolerances for lengths, angles, and numbers can be specified using the (LENGTH_UNITS), (ANGLE_UNITS), and (unitless) keys, respectively. The tolerance for a specific configuration input can be specified using that input name as the key. 
EXAMPLE
{ (LENGTH_UNITS) : 1e-4 * meter, (unitless) : 1e-8, "count" : 0 } causes length configuration variables that differ by less than 1e-4 meters to be considered identical, as well as numberical configuration variables that differ by less than 1e-8, except that configuration variables named "count" are compared exactly.

files.description: A manipulator is an alternative, graphical UI for controlling a feature's definition. For example, in Onshape's extrude feature, the arrow which appears at the end of a blind extrusion is a manipulator controlling the depth parameter. A manipulator can be one of a few ManipulatorTypes, which are generally draggable arrows designed to control different degrees of freedom.

entries.name: makeWrapSurface
entries.description: Make a WrapSurface for opWrap defined by a planar or cylindrical face.

parameters.name: face
parameters.description: A face to use as the definition face for the WrapSurface. For a planar face: The plane origin will be used as the anchorPoint and the plane x direction will be used as the anchorDirection. For a cylindrical face: The point at which the cylinder's coordSystem's positive xAxis intersects the cylinder will be used as the anchorPoint. The cylinder's yAxis will be used as the anchorDirection. See WrapSurface documentation for descriptions of anchorPoint and anchorDirection.

entries.name: makeWrapSurface
entries.signature: (context is Context, face is Query, anchorPoint is Vector, spin is ValueWithUnits)
entries.description: Make a WrapSurface for opWrap defined by a planar, cylindrical or conical face.

parameters.name: face
parameters.description: A face to use as the definition face for the WrapSurface.

parameters.name: anchorPoint
parameters.description: The anchor point of the WrapSurface. See WrapSurface documentation.

parameters.name: spin
parameters.description:
For a planar face: Angle of a counter-clockwise spin to apply to the plane's x axis about its positive z axis, which is then used as the anchorDirection. For a cylindrical face: Angle of a counter-clockwise spin to apply to the cylinder's canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint about the direction vector from the cylinder axis to the anchorPoint. The canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint is defined as the "rightward" direction when looking at the cylinder in the direction from the anchorPoint to the cylinder axis with the cylinder's zAxis up. In other words: cross(cylinder z axis, direction vector from cylinder axis to anchorPoint). This spun direction is then used as the anchorDirection. For a conical face: Angle of a counter-clockwise spin to apply to the cone's canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint about the normal at anchorPoint. The canonical anchorDirection at the given anchorPoint is defined as the "rightward" direction when looking at the cone from the normal.
See WrapSurface documentation for a description of anchorDirection.

entries.name: DraftFeatureType
entries.description: Types of drafts available for the draft feature.

parameters.name: NEUTRAL_PLANE
parameters.type: Draft by holding the intersection between a set of faces and a neutral plane as a constant.

parameters.name: PARTING_LINE
parameters.type: Draft by holding a set of parting edges as a constant.

entries.description: Specifies which faces to draft when drafting with DraftFeatureType.PARTING_LINE.

parameters.name: ONE_SIDED
parameters.type: Draft one of the faces attached to the parting line.

parameters.name: SYMMETRIC
parameters.type: Draft both of the faces attached to the parting line symmetrically.

parameters.name: TWO_SIDED
parameters.type: Draft both of the faces attached to the parting line with separate draft angles.

entries.name: draft
entries.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
entries.description: Feature performing an opDraft.

parameters.name: neutralPlane
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is NEUTRAL_PLANE A planar face or mate connector defining both the neutral plane and pull direction of the the draft. The intersection of the drafted faces and the neutral plane remains unchanged. The pull direction of the draft will be the face normal or mate connector z-axis.

parameters.name: draftFaces
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is NEUTRAL_PLANE The faces to draft for a NEUTRAL_PLANE draft.

parameters.name: pullDirectionEntity
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is PARTING_LINE An entity defining the pull direction of the draft. This entity should conform to the ALLOWS_DIRECTION specification in QueryFilterCompound.

parameters.name: partingEdges
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is PARTING_LINE Edges defining the parting line of the draft. These edges will remain unchanged as some adjacent faces, as defined by partingLineSides, are drafted.

parameters.name: hintFaces
parameters.description: OptionalFor Onshape internal use. For PARTING_LINE draft, specifies in advance which adjacent faces of partingEdges should be treated as more along the pull direction. When unspecified, the feature will use a geometric calculation to determine this distinction.

parameters.name: partingLineSides
parameters.description: Required if draftFeatureType is PARTING_LINE Specifies whether to draft one or both faces adjacent to the parting edges, and whether the draft should be symmetrical if drafting both faces. See PartingLineSides.

parameters.name: alongPull
parameters.description: Required if PartingLineSides is ONE_SIDED Specifies which face will be drafted in a ONE_SIDED PARTING_LINE draft. If true, the face which is more along the pull direction from the perspective of the parting edge is drafted. If false, the face which is more away from the pull direction from the perspective of the parting edge is drafted.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description:
The draft angle, must be between 0 and 89.9 degrees. 
EXAMPLE
3 * degree

parameters.name: pullDirection
parameters.description: OptionalWhether the pull direction of the draft should be reversed. In equivalent terms, whether the draft should use -angle as the draft angle (true), or angle as the draft angle (false). Default is false.

parameters.name: secondAngle
parameters.description:
Required if PartingLineSides is TWO_SIDED The second draft angle for a TWO_SIDED PARTING_LINE draft. Must be between 0 and 89.9 degrees. Note that when using TWO_SIDED, angle will be applied to faces that are away from the pull direction, from the perspective of the edge. secondAngle will be applied to faces that are along the pull direction, from the perspective of the edge. 
EXAMPLE
3 * degree

parameters.name: secondPullDirection
parameters.description: OptionalWhether the pull direction of the draft should be reversed for the second angle of a TWO_SIDED draft. In equivalent terms, whether the draft should use -secondAngle as the second draft angle (true), or secondAngle as the second draft angle (false). Default is false.

parameters.name: tangentPropagation
parameters.description: OptionalFor a NEUTRAL_PLANE draft, true to propagate draft across tangent faces. Default is false.

parameters.name: referenceEdgePropagation
parameters.description: OptionalFor a PARTING_LINE draft, true to extend the parting line across connected edges of already included faces and tangent faces. Default is false.

parameters.name: reFillet
parameters.description: Optionaltrue to attempt to defillet draft faces before the draft and reapply the fillets after. Default is false.

true to add a translational offset from the selected face, surface, solid body or vertex.

false to offset away from the selected second direction end bound (default) EXAMPLE
true to offset into the selected second direction end bound

parameters.name: hasSecondDirectionDraft
parameters.description:
OptionalEXAMPLE
true to add a draft to the second direction extrude.

parameters.name: secondDirectionDraftPullDirection
parameters.description:
OptionalEXAMPLE
false to draft the second direction outwards (default) EXAMPLE
true to draft the second direction inwards

entries.name: sheetMetalCornerBreak
entries.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
entries.description: Sheet metal specific feature combining functionality of edge fillet and chamfer. It calls SMEdgeBlendImpl to apply fillets or chamfers in flat and then change the definition surface accordingly As a result of this change rips corner/bend reliefs are also "baked" into the definition surface and flexibility of sheet metal model is lost. For this reason we recommend that this feature is used after sheet metal flanges, joints and reliefs are finalized.

entries.name: HolePositionReference
entries.description: For a HoleProfile, a reference point along the hole axis to which the position of the profile is relative. To calculate these references, the cylinder of the hole is intersected with the targets of the hole. If the hole cylinder encounters a slanted or otherwise irregular face at the intersection with the target, the reference may by a range rather than a single point. Users may specify that they want the end of this range by using a holeProfile, or the beginning of this range by using a holeProfileBeforeReference; or they may control this behavior directly by setting the beforeReference flag of the HoleProfile.

parameters.name: AXIS_POINT
parameters.type: When calling opHole, the user will supply one or more axes defining where the holes are to be placed. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the origin of the axis Line of the hole.

parameters.name: TARGET_START
parameters.type: When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the closest intersection of the hole cylinder with any target.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_START
parameters.type: For each target, find the first intersection of the hole cylinder into the target. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest of those intersections. Notably, this means that if certain targets are geometrically constructed such that the hole cylinder enters and exits the target multiple times, only the first of the entrances into the target is considered.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_END
parameters.type: When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest exit of the hole cylinder from any target.

parameters.name: LAST_TARGET_START_IN_DEPTH
parameters.type: For each target, find the first intersection of the hole cylinder into the target. When using this reference, the position of the profile will be in reference to the furthest of those intersections within the hole depth.

entries.name: sectionPart
entries.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
entries.description: Feature creating a section of a part behind a plane. Internally, performs an opSplitPart followed by an opDeleteBodies.

entries.name: planeSectionPart
entries.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
entries.description: Split a set of parts with a plane and delete all bodies in front of the face. Unlike sectionPart, bodies which are entirely behind the split plane are retained. Any bodies not included in the target query are deleted.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Bodies to be split.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: Plane that splits the bodies. Everything on the positive z side of the plane will be removed.

entries.name: multiplePlaneSectionPart
entries.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
entries.description: Split a set of parts with multiple planes and delete all bodies in front of the faces.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Bodies to be split.

parameters.name: sketchPlanes
parameters.description: Planes that splits the bodies. Everything on the positive z side of the planes will be removed.

entries.name: multiplePlanesSectionTransformedParts
entries.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
entries.description: method for processing all part studio parts for assembly for multiple planes section

parameters.name: targets
parameters.description: Bodies to be split.

parameters.name: planes
parameters.description: Planes that splits the bodies. Everything on the positive z side of the planes will be removed.

entries.name: jogSectionPart
entries.signature: (context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
entries.description: Split a part down a jogged section line and delete all back bodies. Used by drawings. Needs to be a feature so that drawings created by queries can resolve. Any bodies not included in the target query are deleted.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Bodies to be split.

parameters.name: sketchPlane
parameters.description: Plane that the jog line will be drawn in and extruded normal to. Everything on the positive x side of the jog line will be removed.

parameters.name: jogPoints
parameters.description: Points that the cutting line goes through in world coordinates.

parameters.name: isPartialSection
parameters.description: Whether or not it is a partial section cut.

parameters.name: keepSketches
parameters.description: Whether or not sketches will be kept in the section cut results.

parameters.name: isBrokenOut
parameters.description: Whether or not it is a broken-out section cut.

parameters.name: isCropView
parameters.description: Whether or not it is a crop section cut.

parameters.name: brokenOutPointNumbers
parameters.description: Array of the number of spline points of each broken-out section cut.

parameters.name: brokenOutEndConditions
parameters.description: Array of end conditions of each broken-out section cut.

parameters.name: offsetPoints
parameters.description: Array of points for offsetting the section lines.

parameters.name: isAlignedSection
parameters.description: Whether or not it is an aligned section cut.

entries.name: SMCornerType
entries.description: Specifies the type of corner at a vertex of a sheet metal model.

parameters.name: OPEN_CORNER
parameters.type: The corner has more than two bends or, when folded the edges of the metal do not meet.

parameters.name: CLOSED_CORNER
parameters.type: The corner has two bends and when folded the edge of the metal meet.

parameters.name: BEND_END
parameters.type: The 'corner' is the end of a bend and there may be bend relief.

parameters.name: NOT_A_CORNER
parameters.type: The vertex is not associated with a corner

entries.name: TableTextAlignment

entries.name: TessellatedLoftReturnStatus
entries.description: Enumerates failure modes for tessellated loft.

parameters.name: CRISS_CROSSED_MATCHES
parameters.type: At least two matches cross each other.

parameters.name: UNDERNOURISHED_MATCHES
parameters.type: At least one match consists of fewer than 2 match points.

parameters.name: NON_CONSECUTIVE_MATCHES
parameters.type: A match jumps across a profile without specifying a match point.

parameters.name: MATCHING_CYLINDER_CREATION_FAILED
parameters.type: Most likely due to two profiles touching.

parameters.name: NON_CURVE_INPUT
parameters.type: Only curves are allowed within profiles.

parameters.name: INVALID_MATCH_POINT_INDEX
parameters.type: At least one of the match indices points to a non-existent match point.

parameters.name: INVALID_MATCH_POINT
parameters.type: At least one match point is specified on non-profile topology.

files.description: The tool.fs module contains enum types shared by multiple features.

entries.name: MoveFaceType
entries.description: Defines how face should be transformed in a moveFace feature.

entries.name: ToolBodyType
entries.description: Defines what type of body a body-creating feature (extrude, revolve, etc.) should create.

entries.name: ExtendedToolBodyType
entries.description: Defines what type of body a body-creating feature (extrude, revolve, etc.) should create.

entries.name: NewBodyOperationType
entries.description: Defines how a new body from a body-creating feature (extrude, revolve, etc.) should be merged with other bodies in the context.

parameters.name: NEW
parameters.type: Creates a new body in the context with the geometry resulting from the operation.

parameters.name: ADD
parameters.type: Performs a boolean union between the new body and all bodies in the merge scope.

parameters.name: REMOVE
parameters.type: Performs a boolean subtraction of the new body from all bodies in the merge scope.

parameters.name: INTERSECT
parameters.type: Performs a boolean intersection between each new body and each body in the merge scope.

entries.name: NewSurfaceOperationType
entries.description: Defines how a new surface from a surface-creating feature (sweep, loft, revolve, etc.) should be merged with other surfaces in the context.

parameters.name: NEW
parameters.type: Creates a new surface in the context with the geometry resulting from the operation.

parameters.name: ADD
parameters.type: Performs a surface union between the new surface and all surfaces used as input.

entries.name: UIHint
entries.description: List of available UI Hints, which control how a parameter input is displayed in the feature dialog.

parameters.name: OPPOSITE_DIRECTION
parameters.type: For a boolean parameter, display as a toggle button with arrow next to the previous parameter.

parameters.name: ALWAYS_HIDDEN
parameters.type: Do not display this parameter or allow a user to edit it (useful for parameters changed only in editing logic or manipulator change functions).

parameters.name: SHOW_CREATE_SELECTION
parameters.type: For a query parameter, include a button to open the "Create selection" dialog.

parameters.name: NO_PREVIEW_PROVIDED
parameters.type: For a feature, hide the preview slider which controls before/after transparency, and only show the final version.

parameters.name: REMEMBER_PREVIOUS_VALUE
parameters.type: When a user makes a new instance of this feature, set this parameter's default value to the value they set the last time they used this feature.

parameters.name: DISPLAY_SHORT
parameters.type: Two consecutive boolean or quantity parameters marked as DISPLAY_SHORT may be placed on the same line.

parameters.name: SHOW_EXPRESSION
parameters.type: If an expression (like #foo or 1/4 in) is entered, always show the expression, and never the resulting value.

parameters.name: OPPOSITE_DIRECTION_CIRCULAR
parameters.type: Like OPPOSITE_DIRECTION, but with circular arrows.

parameters.name: SHOW_LABEL
parameters.type: Show a label above an enum parameter.

parameters.name: HORIZONTAL_ENUM
parameters.type: Display an enum as a horizontal list of clickable text, rather than the default select control

parameters.name: MATCH_LAST_ARRAY_ITEM
parameters.type: Inside an array parameter, set the default value on a new item to match what is set on the last item.

parameters.name: COLLAPSE_ARRAY_ITEMS
parameters.type: For an array parameter, create new items (and items in a newly opened dialog) as collapsed by default.

parameters.name: INITIAL_FOCUS_ON_EDIT
parameters.type: When an existing feature is edited, the first visible parameter with this UI hint will get focus.

parameters.name: INITIAL_FOCUS
parameters.type: When creating or editing, the first visible parameter with this UI hint will get focus (but when editing, a parameter with INITIAL_FOCUS_ON_EDIT takes precedence).

parameters.name: READ_ONLY
parameters.type: Prevent changes to the parameter from the feature dialog. A read-only parameter can be modified by the editing logic function.

parameters.name: PREVENT_CREATING_NEW_MATE_CONNECTORS
parameters.type: For a query parameter allowing BodyType.MATE_CONNECTOR, only allow preexisting mate connectors, and don't provide a button to allow creating new mate connectors specificaly for this parameter.

parameters.name: FIRST_IN_ROW
parameters.type: Guarantee that, regardless of other layout requirements, this parameter will always be the first parameter in its displayed row.

parameters.name: ALLOW_QUERY_ORDER
parameters.type: Enable reordering of queries in a query parameter.

parameters.name: PREVENT_ARRAY_REORDER
parameters.type: Disable reordering of items in an array parameter.

parameters.name: FOCUS_INNER_QUERY
parameters.type: When adding a new item to an array parameter, focus the driving inner QLV if the parameter is selection-driven, and focus the first inner QLV otherwise.

parameters.name: SHOW_TOLERANCE
parameters.type: For a boolean parameter, display as a toggle button with tolerance icon next to the previous parameter.

parameters.name: ALLOW_ARRAY_FOCUS
parameters.type: Allow focusing an array parameter with no driving or inner QLV, as if it were selection-driven.

parameters.name: SHOW_INLINE_CONFIG_INPUTS
parameters.type: Inline the configuration parameters in the configure dialog for the feature.

parameters.name: FOCUS_ON_VISIBLE
parameters.type: For a query parameter, selects it when it becomes visible during editing.

parameters.name: CAN_BE_TOLERANT
parameters.type: For a quantity parameter, specifies that the quantity can be tolerant.

parameters.name: CAN_BE_TOLERANT_DIAMETER
parameters.type: For a quantity parameter that represents a diameter, specifies that the quantity can be tolerant and should display options to specify hole or shaft fit classes.

parameters.name: PLUS_MINUS
parameters.type: Like OPPOSITE_DIRECTION but indicating whether the associated quantity is positive or negative.

parameters.name: ALWAYS_USE_DEPENDENCIES
parameters.type: Always use the content of this parameter to determine feature dependencies.

parameters.name: NO_QUERY_VARIABLE
parameters.type: Hides the query variable dropdown for the associated query parameter.

parameters.name: ALLOW_FLAT_SKETCH_SELECTION
parameters.type: Allows a feature list parameter to select sketches defined on flat views.

entries.name: VariableType
entries.description: See assignVariable.

entries.name: VolumeAccuracy
entries.description: Level of accuracy to use for computing the volume of a solid body. The values are:

entries.name: WeldFinishing
entries.description: Enum to determine the weld finishing in ANSI standard.

entries.name: WeldStandard
entries.description: Enum to switch the weld symbol representation between ANSI and ISO standard.

entries.name: WrapType
entries.description: Specifies the type of wrap to execute.

parameters.name: SIMPLE
parameters.type: Wrap around the infinite definition of the destination surface.

parameters.name: TRIM
parameters.type: Wrap around a defined destination face, and trim anything that falls off of it.

parameters.name: IMPRINT
parameters.type: Imprint edges onto a defined destination face.
